signals.text: Revenue grew 15% a year over 3 years vs 16% over 5: growth is steady.
Profit compounded at 40% vs revenue at 15%: operating leverage is showing.
Operating margin expanded 400 bps in 3 years (51.2% → 55.2%).
Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 418% of reported profit: profits are turning into cash.

guidance.statement: Nxtra will need to lever up in order to build out towards the 1 gigawatt target over the next few years.
guidance.quote: the fact is that Nxtra will need to lever up in order to build out what is required over the next few years.

guidance.statement: Airtel Money is preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026.
guidance.quote: Given this growth trajectory and the large addressable opportunity, Airtel Money is now preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026.

guidance.statement: The company is working towards its ambition to build one gigawatt in data centers in the next few years.
guidance.quote: We are working towards our ambition to build one gigawatt in the next few years.

delivered.statement: Consolidated revenue was Rs.58,500 Crores, growing at about 5.7% sequentially.
Consolidated EBITDAaL was at Rs.29,800 Crores, a growth of 4.2% with a margin of 51%.
Capex for the quarter was about Rs.13,390 Crores.
Operating free cash flow was at over Rs.16,450 Crores.
Airtel Business revenue came in at about Rs.5670 Crores, growing 3.2% sequentially.
Mobile segment added 3.3 million revenue earning customers and 5 million smartphone data customers.

calls.tone: Confident on demand and portfolio growth, cautious on industry pricing architecture and homes acquisition quality.

pushback.gist: Analysts probed the allocation of capex towards AI, data centers, subsea cables, and whether to use parent balance sheet versus external funding.
Questions raised on whether moderating home additions and lower margins reflect a conscious slowdown or competitive pressure.
Pressed on sustainability of ARPU growth without a general tariff hike and the timeline for fixing the industry's pricing architecture.
Inquired about the sub-segment drivers of B2B growth, deal conversion cycles in Cloud, and future margin trajectory.

business.summary: Bharti Airtel provides telecommunications, enterprise solutions, home broadband, digital TV, digital services (Cloud, data centers, cybersecurity, IoT), and financial services (Airtel Payments Bank and NBFC lending) across India and Africa.

segments.note: Core mobility and home broadband services.

segments.note: Connectivity, cloud, data centers, and digital services.

guidance.statement: The net capex ballpark will be similar to this year, give or take a little bit.
guidance.quote: our sense is that we will be in the ballpark of this year, give or take a little bit.

guidance.statement: The ambition for data centers is to get to a gigawatt over the next few years.
guidance.quote: our ambition is to get to a gigawatt as we mentioned in a few years’ time

delivered.statement: Consolidated revenue crossed a lifetime high of about Rs.2,11,000 Crores for FY2026.
FY2026 consolidated EBITDAaL margin came in at about 51.2%.
India mobile added 4.7 million customers in Q4, including 5.8 million smartphone customers.
Monthly loan disbursement run rate is now over Rs.550 Crores in financial services.
Airtel Payments Bank annualized revenue run rate reached about Rs.3,400 Crores in Q4.
Homes business added 4.2 million customers during FY2026.

calls.tone: confident on long-term demand and cash flows, cautious on short-term ARPU growth and pricing architecture.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned whether organic growth can continue without tariff hikes given a large base and flat ARPU.
Questions were raised on capital allocation priorities, cash deployment, and potential non-India asset investments.
Analysts inquired about competitive pressures in home broadband and the heavy focus on fiber versus fixed wireless access.
Pushback on when the industry will move to metered data given ongoing unlimited 5G offerings.

guidance.statement: The plan is to reach 1 gigawatt capacity in the next three to four years and grow significantly ahead of the market.
guidance.quote: Our plan is to reach 1 gigawatt capacity in the next three to four years and grow significantly ahead of the market.

delivered.statement: Consolidated revenue came in at about Rs.54,000 crores, growing 3.5% sequentially.
EBITDAaL margin stood at 51.3%, about 30 basis points improvement sequentially.
Operating free cash flow was a strong Rs.15,900 crores with capex at about Rs.11,800 crores.
India mobility added 4.4 million revenue earning customers and 5.2 million smartphone data consumers.
Broadband delivered highest ever quarterly net adds of 1.2 million customers, crossing 13 million connected homes.
Digital portfolio delivered robust revenue growth and grew 39% over last year.

calls.tone: confident on demand, cautious on margins, and focused on disciplined capital allocation and digital growth

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned wireless revenue growth falling below 10% and whether tariff repair is necessary.
Pressured on upcoming AGR payments, lack of DoT parity response, and cash flow pressures.
Questions raised on very low net debt to EBITDA and whether surplus capital should be returned via special dividends.
Inquired about differentiated pricing between 4G and 5G and network slicing regulations.

guidance.statement: Capex will directionally moderate over time.
guidance.quote: directionally, it should moderate over time.

guidance.statement: Nxtra aims to reach over 1 gigawatt in the next few years, a 4x capacity increase.
guidance.quote: gives us a clear visibility to get to over 1 gigawatt in the next few years. This is a four-fold increase from our operating capacity currently.

delivered.statement: Consolidated revenues reached about 52,000 Crores with an annualized run rate over Rs.200,000 Crores.
India EBITDAaL margin excluding passive infra came in at 51.5%.
India operating free cash flow was Rs.10,750 Crores and capex was about Rs.7,200 Crores.
Mobile segment added 1.4 million revenue earning customers and 5.1 million smartphone data users.
Broadband business reported net adds of 951,000, with FWA base crossing 2.3 million.
Airtel Business reported revenues of about Rs.5,275 Crores, growing 4.3% sequentially.

calls.tone: Confident on demand and digital scaling, disciplined on capital allocation, and optimistic about convergence.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned applicability and next steps regarding the Supreme Court AGR reconciliation order.
Pressured on the massive potential scale of investments and funding for the 1 GW data center target.
Asked about elevated home broadband capex per customer and whether FWA causes capacity issues.
Questioned the rationale and future strategy behind increasing the equity stake in Indus Towers.

guidance.statement: Public capital expenditure was raised to ₹12.2 trillion for FY2026-27.
guidance.quote: Public capital expenditure was raised to ₹12.2 trillion for FY2026-27, up from ₹11 trillion in FY2025-26.

guidance.statement: India's real GDP growth is projected at 6.6% for FY 2026-27.
guidance.quote: Real GDP growth is projected at 6.6% for FY 2026-27.

guidance.statement: Global headline inflation is projected at around 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027.
guidance.quote: global headline inflation projected at around 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027

guidance.statement: Global growth is projected at around 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.
guidance.quote: Global growth is projected at around 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027

delivered.statement: Delivered record-high revenue of ₹1,214,927 million in FY 2025-26, marking an 11.5% increase.
EBITDAaL margins in FY 2025-26 improved to 51.4% compared to 49.0% in the previous year.
Net Profit before exceptional items & tax (PBT) increased to ₹227,916 million.
5G customer base has grown to 188 million.
Consolidated revenues for the year ended March 31, 2026 stood at ₹2,109,728 million.
Capital expenditure for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, was ₹475,218 million.

calls.tone: Confident and disciplined, focusing on strong execution, digital acceleration, cost discipline, and robust financial performance.
